title: A Mountain Trap, Coupled With a Disaster
desc:
A barrage of fire, an artillery cannonade, the cries of pain from the soldiers of his Black Guard - all of this forced the fighters of the Black League, cut off from their capital, to retreat whilst still fighting. News of the fall of Omsk arrived four days late, by which time the divisions under Savintsev's command had been completely driven out of the city of Sverdlovsk. Reading the latest telegram from headquarters, it became clear that the situation had spiralled out of control and had become catastrophic. Pavel Batov's insurgents were successfully capturing town after town, region after region, and pushing the remnants of the League ever further back, even without being adequately armed.

In Yevgeny's view, the actions of his comrade, the Glakoverkh, simply could not have led to this catastrophe; no, that was out of the question, and he immediately dismissed such thoughts from his mind. Moreover, the majority of the generals were also loyal, which suggests only one explanation for this horror for the League. It was the number of traitors; it briefly exceeded the number of soldiers and the entire Black League army. Visibly on edge after a gruelling, unrelenting two-day retreat, he, together with his Spetsgruppa 'V', loyal and well-armed units of the Black Guard, and several exhausted Redemptive Brigades, reached the centre of the settlement of Saranpaul.

In the coming months, this will form the main foundation for the League’s revival, under his personal command. Let everyone know that the fight against separatists and traitors is not over and will be seen through to the end! Fortunately, we are not alone in our cause, for that undying dog Batov shares a border with another remnants of the League - Task Force 'Bogatyr', which has successfully established itself in Zlatoust. This will help us buy time to plan and prepare for our grand campaign to save Omsk from anarchy and to recapture our entire operational base in Western Siberia.

title: Further Trials of Fate With the New Glakoverkh
desc:
Yet another evening without light in this mountain trap, yet another glass of vodka downed, yet another hangover for Yazov’s former ‘right-hand man’. As he tried to quell the signs of depression with this alcoholic drink, Yevgeny felt no relief; on the contrary, he felt anger at this dreadful situation for the League and its ideas, which would become harder and harder to put into practice with each passing day. Of course, whilst we stand still, our enemies are stockpiling weapons and advancing technologically. The League, meanwhile, already set back years in this regard, has been driven into a corner by the affliction of its people, known as 'Russian anarchy'.

At such moments, the leader of Spetsgruppa 'V' would often feel sick to his stomach; he was disgusted by what Russian society had become after two decades of disunity. "The Russians are already losing out to the national minorities inhabiting their territory and are suffering from acts of treachery.. at the hands of the Teutons", thought Savintsev. And then he came to his senses, reaching a perfectly logical, not entirely new conclusion in the spirit of his Black League. They were simply continuing to reap the fruits of the Nazi victory in the Second World War. So the only solution would be to fight, to fight in order to hasten his revenge and the Great Trial, which his spiritual mentor Dmitry had so desperately wanted to carry out.

..."Evgeny. Your skill and devotion to the Black League have set you apart from your fellow officers, and in the days to come, we will all be put to the test. Do you accept this task?"... - Guided by this praise from Yazov, which was etched in his heart, he came to realise this new mission and the responsibility that now rested on his shoulders. From now on, it was his destiny to become the new Glakoverkh, the leader of the Great Trial. He continues to enjoy complete authority amongst the soldiers of the Black League beyond Saranpaul, so, wasting no time, he will begin to put his future plans into action, drawing on the guidance of the late former Glakoverkh.

In memory of him and his ideals, he must defeat all the traitors and scum who overthrew the centralised authority in Omsk. New military campaigns and wars with neighbouring separatist entities - which currently exist in Western Siberia - are on the horizon. There will be no mercy shown to them, just as they showed no mercy to their former masters. The Black League has not fallen; the thirst for revenge and hatred still burns within its loyal soldiers, and the generals are ready to take their revenge under the leadership of their new Glakoverkh - Yevgeny Savintsev.

title: 'From Saranpaul, in revenge for Yazov'
desc:
As he reread the letter, which was intended to authorise the next military operations, Yevgeny counted on his fingers how much time he had left. Often relieving his stress with a cigarette rather than drowning it in a glass of vodka, he tried to anticipate the actions of his enemies and the traitors from Sverdlovsk. The issue was not that he feared death should the enemies crush the last remnants of the Black League, but rather the Russian people's yet another failure in their preparations for the Great Trial. The Teutons were far stronger and far better prepared than the Russians, who lagged behind them by decades.

At the same time, he had no intention of deviating from Yazov's plans regarding the nuclear doctrine, which his predecessor had outlined to him shortly before his death. Everything had to be done in time - reach agreements with the Task Force 'Bogatyr' to prevent a split, promptly crush the rebellious separatist groups and all of Batov's allies in Western Siberia, and build up the army as much as possible. However, for the time being, the focus was on dispersing forces across various fronts, including the delivery of weapons to Zlatoust. If the negotiations were successful, they would have to advance from different directions and capture Nizhny Tagil. Following this crucial victory, their position and preparedness would improve significantly.

"Our esteemed soratnik (comrade-in-arms) Konstantin, we are counting on your brigades to take the same decision as ours - to crush the Chekists. We are prepared to supply you with all the necessary weaponry in exchange for your recognition of our control over this city and region. We will not stop, and whilst you are blockaded by traitors in the south, we will completely clear the north-east of Western Siberia. When the time comes, both we and you will have sufficient strength to complete the work begun by the honourable Dmitry Timofeyevich Yazov. Remember the oath of the Black League: this is a time for unity and for hated vengeance against our enemies. Glory to the Black League, the liberators!" - the Glakoverkh read his letter aloud once more. Indeed, this letter corresponded to his summons; now it is a matter of ensuring the safe delivery of this letter by our agents through the enemy territory of the so-called People's Republic of Nizhny Tagil.

Failure is not an option, so we shall specifically entrust this important mission to the native inhabitants of the city of Nizhny Tagil, who have remained loyal to the League's cause to this day. Having successfully completed this mission and returned to their city, these infiltrators will await their liberation and the promotion they deserve within the ranks of the Black Guard.

Dark and bloody days lie ahead for all insurgent movements, for from now on their existence is merely a matter of time, depending on the pace of our military operations.

title: The Triumphant
desc:
Following the protracted months of anarchy that followed the collapse of the Black League’s centralised authority and the death of Dmitry Yazov, today was a long-awaited day for the residents of Omsk. The era of looting, pillaging and anarchy is coming to an end with the arrival in the city of the exhausted military units of the new Black League. The parade has been going on for several hours now; no one is sleeping, and the city’s central squares are packed with people. No one will dare to continue stealing from and plundering the capital of the state, driven by hatred of disorder and treachery, for at best they will face torment in prisons with excessive hard labour, and at worst – execution without trial or investigation.

Standing proudly in his car, which had been manufactured in Zlatoust, their respected Glakoverkh and liberator, Yevgeny Savintsev, waved to the crowd, prompting applause and cheers. He promises to give these people everything they need to continue working towards the common national goal – the destruction of the existing Teutons. They will be issued with free clothing and, on occasion, even food, whilst community service will be encouraged, funded by military spoils. All luxury goods will soon be nationalised, and at the earliest opportunity, nuclear weapons will be researched to ensure the survival of his regime.

In the years to come, there is a high probability of direct conflict with the Teutons, so all citizens – with the exception of certain categories of women and the infirm elderly – will serve for several years in the army. Constant external threats will persist, so funding for state propaganda must be maintained without interruption. Furthermore, private banks will be required to pay high taxes amounting to a quarter of their assets every six months; otherwise, they too will be nationalised.

As he rounded yet another bend in the road and forced a smile, Savintsev, without giving a thought to the consequences, was already planning the next round of necessary purges for the very next day. Hatred and a thirst for revenge would continue to simmer in Omsk and spread throughout Russia; only under these conditions, in Savintsev’s view, would the Russian people be capable of overcoming the Aryan spirit. The Teutonic threat would either be eliminated or triumph in its accursed 'Endsieg', all Russians must be aware of this.

A stop; the deserted courtyard of the Glavkovverh’s residence in Omsk; the engine switched off. Presumably, the only public day of light in the state has come to an end; it will be followed by malice, anger, repression, and constant training and national service for the Black League. But for success, the whole of Russia must yet be reunited, and all possible resources – including those not currently available – will be allocated to this end, whilst all traitors and opponents of the Black League on Russian territory will undoubtedly be punished.

title: Pressing the two red buttons...
desc:
The seemingly endless meat grinder has come to an end; the Revengeful Russian National State has lost the Great Trial. The Russian people, driven solely by hatred and vengeance, had sealed their fate forever. And so, at last, the entire general staff of the Black League - those who had not been taken prisoner or killed - were gathered here, including Alexander Lazarenko. All agreed with the Glavkoverkh's assertion that this world could no longer be saved.

All the superpowers seized the moment to grab a slice of our Motherland for themselves. The Teutons took Europe as far as the Urals, Japan took Central Asia, and the USA took all our key Pacific ports. It was not merely the partition of Russia; it was her demise as a state… forever. Yet in Savintsev's hands loomed the red button to launch all the nuclear warheads he had stockpiled during his reign. Barely half of the total pre-war stockpile remained, but that was enough for him.

Glancing at his loyal generals, he saw the resolve in their eyes - just like him, they had long since made up their minds. The second red button had been pressed several hours earlier; now it was his turn. Eleven hours - that was how long it would take for the missiles from Novosibirsk to strike all the key, densely populated cities of the Reich, wiping the Teutons from the face of the earth. However, the Teutons' nuclear triad promised to deliver the same response to all Russians, but that didn't matter. The chosen ones were already in their bunkers, and there was still about one day left to enjoy their last overcast day on the surface.

The Glavkoverkh pressed the button; instantly, a hundred miles from their headquarters, underground hatches opened, from which intercontinental ballistic missiles carrying nuclear warheads emerged. Amidst the deafening roar of their engines, they gradually emerged from the horizon of the Eurasian hills and hurtled west or east. The irreversible process had been set in motion; the Black League was responding to the world with its own destruction, whilst its elite and government descended underground as quickly as possible, without wasting a single minute. In an hour or two, German nuclear warheads would fly in response, followed by Japanese ones... The mutual exchange of missiles would not last long, and after that the earth would rest for a good hundred years from the unrelenting civilisation of this old world...

title: The Redoubt begins with the youth
desc:
The best profession an ordinary citizen could choose - especially following the end of the Teutonic bombings and the fratricidal wars in the region - was that of a builder. All the more so as the national programme for the construction of redoubts opened up significant prospects. Vladimir, a native of Kurgan, was already an experienced builder who had decided to switch sides to the Black League following the unification of Western Siberia. He was assigned an orphaned boy from the town of Tara as his assistant, and it was there that he set off. The journey was far from easy, as the roads were riddled with craters from artillery fire, left behind by various rebels and traitors to the Motherland. Upon arrival, he made his way to the house where he would be staying for the coming months; on the way, he spotted a hill 130 metres from the mighty Irtysh River, which serves as a natural defence for the capital.

Opening the door to the house and seeing a young man named Timofey, he greeted him and made his way to the table, where the planning maps were already laid out. After checking the distances from the edges to the centre, his calculations showed a 20-metre passage to the Redoubt and a height of 5 metres - a relatively small structure. But recalling a similar one—and even a slightly larger one - which had been built back in his younger days in Tyumen, where he had trained, he felt a sense of relief and let out a sigh. Timofey was the first to speak.

"Soratnik Vladimir, your predecessor Arseny, who was supposed to start the clearance work, has been redeployed to Isilkul, to the south, so this section has remained completely untouched from the very beginning. We may run into problems with a shortage of staff, as there are only the two of us, and what’s more, I have no experience in this field."

"Really? Well, consider yourself very lucky to have me, because I'm very familiar with similar blueprints, which were built long before we met in 1960. Yes, back then I was the same age as you are now, helping out and carrying out minor tasks related to that construction project. A bunker like this was built on the outskirts of Tyumen, and was intended to protect the Communist Party leadership from German bombing raids - can you imagine?" Vladimir said, with a touch of irony in his voice.

Timofey hadn't quite grasped the full meaning of his superior's words, but, scratching the back of his head, he said: "Still, this isn't Tyumen, and the local redoubt isn't needed to defend against conventional bombing, but against a potential nuclear attack. I went to school in Omsk, and I was clearly briefed on all the threats posed by such an attack, which is in a completely different league to conventional bombing. So anyway, we need to start looking for assistants and materials, also - " Before he could finish his objection, Vladimir cut him off.

"Not quite. I was going to say that the higher-ups already know about the projects I've been working on outside Omsk. That's precisely why I'll be able to arrange for that bunker in Tyumen to be moved here, and all we'll have to do is simply refit it, and it'll be ready in a month or two - isn't that brilliant?"

Right up to the last moment, Timofey couldn't bring himself to believe that this time he wouldn't have to work himself to the point of losing consciousness - something he'd, on the whole, already resigned himself to. Perhaps this was his only chance to find a foothold, a stroke of luck that would finally see him land a stable and promising job, thanks to which he could forget about poverty or having no roof over his head? The secret dream he had hidden deep in his soul might just begin to come true.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Remnants of the Black League Unifies West Siberia!
desc:
Urgent news is coming from the conflict-torn lands of Western Siberia, which until recently had once again been torn apart by internal resistance movements. The remnants of the Black League, united under Spetsgruppa V - which to the inattentive observer might have seemed a failed state, trampled and destroyed by Batov's uprising - have risen from the ashes. Thanks to the coordinated efforts of the field generals, united under the leadership of a new, ambitious Glakoverkh, they have succeeded once more.

title: [Get_newspaper_header]The Black League Marches On
desc:
Having suffered global humiliations and military setbacks in less than half a century, the Russian people, quite predictably, became radicalised. Today, to thunderous applause and cheers from the soldiers of the 'Chernaya Gvardiya' and ordinary citizens, Yevgeny Alexandrovich Savintsev proclaimed in Omsk a 'Russian revival aimed at putting an end to national humiliation through revenge'.

Savintsev was a dark horse during Yazov's short-lived rule, and now, as Glakoverkh, he personally makes all the key decisions in the country. In reality, however, German intelligence is bold in its assumptions that the leadership of the Black League is multi-layered, much like the predatory Hydra. And although the new state's future plans involve challenging German dominance in Eastern Europe, the Germans are confident of their invincibility. From Chukotka to the Volga, the earth is splitting apart with fury, and the rivers seem to be flowing in the opposite direction altogether. A dark shadow has fallen over Russia, and it's not with the aim of peaceful coexistence with its neighbours.
